content.thinking:
I'm going to return a structured result, so I'm reading through the document first. It's a Chinese delivery note from Dongguan Precision Housings, number SN-260922-508 and dated 22 September 2026, addressed to a distribution center in Hamburg under purchase order 4500318706. The line item is a die-cast statue, CMP-GAM-010, with a quantity listed in German/Polish number style.

I'm reading the quantity and weights on the delivery note now. The 11.500 figure looks like it could mean 11,500 pieces, but 198 kg across 11 packages makes that doubtful for small die-cast statues, so I'm treating the number cautiously and noting the tension.

I'm weighing whether the quantity should be read as 11,500 or something else, since 198 kg across 11 packages doesn't fit with that many small statues. The "11" package count is partly covered by the stamp, but it still lines up with the number printed in the packaging column, so I'll treat it as clear while noting the overlap. The description is cut off after the product's size, so I'll record it as incomplete. As for the dates, the 27.10.2026 receipt stamp is clear, but nothing on the note says when it shipped, so I won't invent a shipping date.

I'm weighing the receiving stamp and the signature on the note, and I'm leaning toward listing them as stamp and handwritten marks rather than as corrections, since neither changes any figure.

I'm settling on a status of has_warnings, since the quantity and weight don't square, and I'm putting the confidence at medium. The remark about moisture and not turning it upside down goes in as a statement, and no acceptance decision is being made, so decisions stay empty. For the references I'm noting the PO number and delivery note number along with the languages, Chinese and English, and the issuer and recipient details.

I'm noting the weight at 198 kg and the package count of 11, both printed on the note, and I'm also checking the carrier, Nordhav Shipping A/S. Next I'm setting the line item to CMP-GAM-010 as the material ID, with no supplier part number.

verdict.summary_en: Chinese-language delivery note SN-260922-508 dated 2026-09-22 from Dongguan Precision Housings to Soony DC Hamburg, for PO 4500318706. It lists one line, CMP-GAM-010 Statue "The Getaway", quantity 11.500 PCS in 11 packages, gross weight 198 kg, carried by Nordhav Shipping A/S. It carries a receiving stamp "RECEIVED 27.10.2026 DC-HAM" and a handwritten signature "Yilmaz D.". There are no strike-throughs or handwritten changes to values. No shortage or damage is noted.
red_flags: Quantity "11.500" is read as 11,500 PCS, assuming the dot is a thousands separator. That is about 17 g per piece for 198 kg. This looks implausible for die-cast statues, so the quantity should be checked against the PO and the physical count.
The part description is cut off at "(die-cast, 18", so the size or specification is not fully visible.
The receiving stamp and signature carry no quantity check, no condition note and no acceptance statement. The stamp shows only a date.
observations: The red round supplier seal overlaps the table headers (单位, 件数) and the edge of the PCS and packages cells. The packages value "11" is partly covered, but it is readable and matches the "件数: 11" below the table.
The item description is truncated at the cell edge.
The blue rectangular stamp is tilted but legible: "RECEIVED 27.10.2026" with "DC-HAM" below it.
The receiver signature "Yilmaz D." is handwritten in blue ink.
A barcode is printed at the top right. The lower half of the page is blank.
The decimal convention for "11.500" is ambiguous on a Chinese-language document with a German consignee.
